```{python}
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import wilcoxon, mannwhitneyu, kruskal
from statsmodels.stats.multitest import multipletests
from scipy.stats import spearmanr
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
from statsmodels.stats.outliers_influence import variance_inflation_factor
```

```{python}
data_filtered = pd.read_csv("data_filtered.csv", index_col=0)
genes_metadata = pd.read_csv("tcga_brca_gene_metadata.csv",index_col=0)
meta_sub = pd.read_csv("sample_metadata_with_subtype.csv",index_col=1)
data_paired = pd.read_csv("data_paired.csv",index_col=0)
sample_paired = pd.read_csv("sample_paired.csv",index_col=0)
fao_score = pd.read_csv("fao_score.csv", index_col=0)  
icr_df = pd.read_csv("icr_df.csv",index_col=0 )
```

```{python}
# Map Ensembl IDs to gene symbols 
data_filtered["gene_symbol"] = data_filtered.index.map(genes_metadata["gene_name"])
data_filtered = data_filtered.dropna(subset=["gene_symbol"])
data_filtered = data_filtered.drop_duplicates(subset="gene_symbol", keep="first")
data_filtered = data_filtered.set_index("gene_symbol")
```

### In Basal-like tumors, are PHGDH and PSAT1 higher in the FAO-low (immune-cold) group? in earlier work, FAO-low Basal tumors were the glycolytic, hypoxic, proliferative ones, so serine synthesis should be higher there if it belongs to the same program.

```{python}
# log2 CPM from the full filtered counts
cpm_all = data_filtered.div(data_filtered.sum(axis=0), axis=1) * 1e6
logcpm_all = np.log2(cpm_all + 1)

tum = meta_sub[(meta_sub["tcga.cgc_sample_sample_type"] == "Primary Tumor") &
               meta_sub["BRCA_Subtype_PAM50"].isin(["Basal", "Her2", "LumA", "LumB"])]
tum = tum[tum.index.isin(logcpm_all.columns)]
```

```{python}
fao = fao_score["Fatty acid oxidation"]                    # a Series indexed by barcode
print(fao.head(3))
print("Scores:", len(fao), "| barcode example:", fao.index[0])

basal_ids = tum.index[tum["BRCA_Subtype_PAM50"] == "Basal"].intersection(fao.index)
print("Basal tumors with an FAO score:", len(basal_ids))     # expect close to 197

fao_b = fao.loc[basal_ids]
hi = fao_b >= fao_b.median()                                 # median split inside Basal
print("FAO-high:", hi.sum(), "| FAO-low:", (~hi).sum())

for g in ["PHGDH", "PSAT1", "SFXN1", "SHMT2", "MTHFD2"]:
    v = logcpm_all.loc[g, basal_ids]
    rho, p = spearmanr(fao_b, v)
    print(f"{g}: rho with FAO = {rho:.2f} (p={p:.3g}); "
          f"median FAO-low {v[~hi].median():.2f} vs FAO-high {v[hi].median():.2f}")
```

High serine synthesis is a **property of the Basal subtype as a whole** (about 20-fold for PSAT1 versus luminal), and it does not vary with the FAO split inside Basal.

```{python}
icr_score = icr_df["icr_score"]    
# fao_b: FAO score for the 197 Basal tumors (from the last step)
# icr_score: your ICR score per tumor, a Series indexed by barcode  <- change to your object name
serine_genes = ["PHGDH", "PSAT1", "PSPH"]
ex = logcpm_all.loc[serine_genes, basal_ids]
serine = ((ex.sub(ex.mean(axis=1), axis=0)).div(ex.std(axis=1), axis=0)).mean(axis=0)

df = pd.DataFrame({"FAO": fao_b, "serine": serine,
                   "ICR": icr_score.reindex(basal_ids)}).dropna()
print("Tumors:", len(df))

# 1) continuous model with interaction (z-scored predictors)
for c in ["FAO", "serine"]:
    df[c + "_z"] = (df[c] - df[c].mean()) / df[c].std()
m = smf.ols("ICR ~ FAO_z * serine_z", data=df).fit()
print(m.summary().tables[1])

# 2) 2x2 groups for display
df["FAO_grp"] = np.where(df["FAO"] >= df["FAO"].median(), "FAO-high", "FAO-low")
df["ser_grp"] = np.where(df["serine"] >= df["serine"].median(), "serine-high", "serine-low")
df["group"] = df["FAO_grp"] + " / " + df["ser_grp"]
print(df.groupby("group")["ICR"].agg(["median", "count"]).round(2))
print("Kruskal across 4 groups: p =", round(kruskal(*[g["ICR"] for _, g in df.groupby("group")]).pvalue, 4))

# 3) the key comparison: within FAO-low, does high serine lower ICR further?
lo = df[df["FAO_grp"] == "FAO-low"]
a = lo.loc[lo["ser_grp"] == "serine-high", "ICR"]
b = lo.loc[lo["ser_grp"] == "serine-low", "ICR"]
print(f"Within FAO-low: serine-high median {a.median():.2f} vs serine-low {b.median():.2f}, "
      f"p = {mannwhitneyu(a, b).pvalue:.3f}")
```

The data does not support a “combination” effect: FAO and serine each relate to immune score independently, and their effects simply add.

```{python}
from scipy.stats import skew
print(df["ICR"].describe().round(2))
print("skew:", round(skew(df["ICR"]), 2))

# rank-based version of the same model (robust to outliers and skew)
df["ICR_rank"] = df["ICR"].rank(pct=True)
m_rank = smf.ols("ICR_rank ~ FAO_z * serine_z", data=df).fit()
print(m_rank.summary().tables[1])
```

In Basal-like TCGA tumors, FAO and serine-synthesis expression are independently associated with immune score, in opposite directions.

```{python}
scores = pd.read_csv("basal_estimate_scores.gct", sep="\t", skiprows=2, index_col=0)
scores = scores.drop(columns=["Description"]).T
scores.columns = ["StromalScore", "ImmuneScore", "ESTIMATEScore"]

# make barcodes match the expression data
scores.index = scores.index.str.replace(".", "-", regex=False)
print("Scores:", len(scores), "| example:", scores.index[0])
print("Overlap with the 197 Basal tumors:", len(df.index.intersection(scores.index)))   # expect ~197

df["stromal"] = scores["StromalScore"].reindex(df.index)
df["immune"] = scores["ImmuneScore"].reindex(df.index)
d = df.dropna(subset=["stromal", "immune"]).copy()
for c in ["stromal", "immune"]:
    d[c + "_z"] = (d[c] - d[c].mean()) / d[c].std()
print("Tumors in adjusted models:", len(d))

m1 = smf.ols("ICR_rank ~ FAO_z + serine_z", data=d).fit()                         # unadjusted, same tumors
m2 = smf.ols("ICR_rank ~ FAO_z + serine_z + stromal_z", data=d).fit()              # main
m3 = smf.ols("ICR_rank ~ FAO_z + serine_z + stromal_z + immune_z", data=d).fit()   # strict

for name, m in [("unadjusted", m1), ("+ stromal", m2), ("+ stromal + immune", m3)]:
    print(f"{name:20s} FAO: {m.params['FAO_z']:+.3f} (p={m.pvalues['FAO_z']:.3g})   "
          f"serine: {m.params['serine_z']:+.3f} (p={m.pvalues['serine_z']:.3g})")
```

Within Basal-like tumors (n = 197), FAO score was positively associated with ICR score, independently of stromal and immune infiltration (adjusted for stromal score: +0.12 percentile units per SD, p = 2e-09; additionally adjusted for immune score: +0.05, p = 4e-06). Expression of serine synthesis genes (PHGDH, PSAT1, PSPH) was associated with lower ICR in unadjusted analysis (-0.05, p = 0.009), but not after adjusting for stromal score (-0.02, p = 0.41), and there was no FAO × serine interaction (p = 0.67).
